title: Alabama missing child or murder case? Why a father and daughter's trial are delayed - NewsBreak
text:
By Avery Boyce ,
25 minutes ago
FAYETTE, Ala ( WIAT ) – The trial for a father and daughter accused of gruesome crimes involving a 1-year-old boy remains on hold nearly a year after the child’s disappearance.
John Bailey, the grandfather of 1-year-old Khaleb Rowan Collins was scheduled for a plea hearing Wednesday. Judge Samuel Junkin told the court one of three things happen in a plea hearing: defendant pleads guilty, the case goes to trial, or the case is continued.
Bailey’s attorneys requested the last option.
While the defense filed the motion, the state is not ready for trial, and investigators have not given a clear answer on whether or not Kahleb remains unaccounted for, or if his remains have been found.
“I do not have any anything before me at this point that suggest Khaleb has been found,” District Attorney Andy Hamlin said.
A family was changed forever after tragedy unfolded on a county road in Fayette.
The Bailey family were in a car headed somewhere – their destination unclear – but they were less than a mile away from home when they crashed into a tree. The young daughter died in the back seat, and the father died at the hospital where the mother, Pam Bailey, was fighting for her life.
Flash forward to Nov. 12, 2025. Bailey and her father John Bailey sit in a Fayette County Jail cell waiting for their case to be heard.
“I think it’s customary in a case of this magnitude,” Hamlin said.
The FCSO learned there should have been a second child in the car the day of the crash – Khaleb. However, the 1-year-old boy was nowhere to be found.
Trump signs funding bill to end historic government shutdown Soon after, John Bailey was arrested for failing to report his grandchild missing.
Family and community members pleaded for Kahleb’s safe return . But text messages and photos revealed Khaleb was tormented and abused by his own parents.
Investigators have not given a clear timeline of when the search shifted from finding Khaleb alive to finding his body; but in May, the FCSO admitted human remains were found on John Bailey’s property and the remains were sent to a state lab for identification.
“As soon as all of the evidence is back and we’re able to go to trial, the state will be seeking to try the case,” Hamlin said.
Hamlin would not say if an I.D. on the human remains in the last piece of the puzzle the state is waiting on.
Pam Bailey has a plea hearing set for April 16.
As of Wednesday, a new plea hearing was not set for John Bailey.
Neither defendant has received a plea deal, and it could be another year before their cases go to tria,l Hamlin said.
